name: Howie Pincus
why: His freshman class portrait, taken two years before his term. It is the only photograph of him the digitised volumes carry as a single frame.

Left-to-right order is fixed by the rows either side: the Fifth Row reads woman, woman, woman, man, man, man, man and the Seventh Row man, woman, man, woman, man, woman, man, and both grids match their lists exactly. name: Donna Porter
why: The only photograph of her in the digitised volumes. She never sat for a class portrait: the 1972 back index gives her pp. 2 and 368 and no class grid carries her. Cropped from a four-figure photograph, so the face is small and soft; it has not been enlarged.
caption_quote: Class officers are Donna Porter, vice president; Cathi Stillwell, secretary; Mike Fiorella, president
how_identified: 1972 Talisman, printed p. 368 (scan leaf n371), the sophomore class spread headed 'Fiorella provides leadership for 2,170-member sophomore class'. Four figures are around a tree and the caption names four. Two things fix which woman is which, and a predecessor who left this frame uncut had only the first. First, the same four names are printed twice on the page in two different orders: the body text runs president, vice-president, secretary, treasurer, which is office rank, while the picture caption runs Porter, Stillwell, Fiorella, Day, which is neither rank nor alphabetical, so it can only be position in the frame, left to right, with '(seated)' appended to explain why Day is last when he is sitting on the grass below the others. That reads Porter as the leftmost and highest figure, a fair-haired woman standing on a branch. Second, and independently, Cathi Stillwell's own class portrait from p. 387 of this same volume shows dark chin-length hair with a centre part turning inward at the jaw, which matches the second woman and not the first: the first has long straight light hair well past the shoulders. The two lines of evidence agree. On the namesake point, the 1972 back index carries exactly one Donna Porter, 'Porter, Donna Jo, 2, 368', and routes her to this page; the second Donna Porter in the record, entered 'Porter, Donna M. S.' in the 1973 and 1974 indexes, is absent from the 1972 volume and carries no page numbers in either of the others. The identification rests on the caption naming the sophomore class vice president, which is the office the worklist gives her, not on the surname.

name: Hamp Moore
why: A working photograph of him on senior class business, and the best frame of him in the digitised volumes. He never sat for a class portrait: the 1974 and 1975 back indexes both enter him as Moore, Frank Hampton and give him p. 282 alone, which is the Sigma Alpha Epsilon membership roster. His eyes are cast down at the papers; no frame exists in which they are not.
caption_quote: Senior class President Carl Stoltzfus confers with Vice-President Hamp Moore over planned activities.
how_identified: 1974 Talisman, printed p. 342 (scan leaf n345), the senior class spread headed 'Senior-itis'. Two men stand at a table and the caption names two, Stoltzfus then Moore. Which is which is settled from outside the frame: Carl Stoltzfus's own class portrait, already published in this archive from p. 387 of the 1972 volume, shows straight light blond hair in a shoulder-length cut with a side sweep, and that is the man on the left. The man on the right has dark, shorter hair and a heavier build, so he is Hamp Moore, and the caption's order is left to right. The page's body text names the same pair in the same roles: 'Heading the senior class were President Carl Stoltzfus and Vice-president Hamp Moore.' The 1974 index carries one Frank Hampton Moore and one Frank Hayden Moore, and only the first is a senior in 1973-74.

name: Scott Taylor
why: The clearest of the two group frames of him in the volume. The other, the Pi Kappa Alpha photograph on p. 288, puts eleven people in one front row around a car with further members on the hood and behind the wheel, and cannot be counted safely.

how_identified: 1976 Talisman, printed p. 333 (scan leaf n336), the Alpha Phi Omega group photograph. The caption gives three rows of exactly four, four and three names, and the photograph has three tiers whose head heights separate cleanly: four men seated cross-legged on the grass, four standing behind them, and three standing highest at the back, staggered into the gaps of the row in front. Taylor is third and last in the back row, so he is the rightmost of the three highest figures, a bearded man with dark curly hair. The 1976 back index puts exactly one Taylor on p. 333, 'Taylor, Thomas Scott 63, 288, 333', so the caption's Tom Taylor is him. The same index entry ties him to student government twice over: p. 63 is the Associated Student Government attendance roll, which prints him as Scott Taylor, and the Pi Kappa Alpha text on p. 288 says in as many words that Pike member Scott Taylor served as a representative to the Associated Student Government.

name: Brad Ford

The man on the right has dark curly hair and a moustache and is plainly not Grizzell, so he is Brad Ford, and the caption's order is left to right. The 1978 back index carries one Bradley Scott Ford, at pp. 33-4 and 323, and no other Ford on p. 33.

name: Jeff Cashdollar

The middle tier is the caption's second row and confirms the reading, because its names run Mark Anderson, Terry Reber, Jerry Wilson, Sharon McKeand, Kathleen Rutherford, Richard Stout, that is man, man, man, woman, woman, man, and the six faces in that tier are man with glasses, man with glasses and a moustache, man with glasses, woman with long light hair, woman with long blonde hair, man, in exactly that order. The 1975 and 1976 indexes each carry one Cashdollar, Jeffrey James, and the 1976 entry is p. 63, the Associated Student Government attendance roll.

name: John Burden
why: A working photograph of him in the psychology laboratory, and the only frame of him the digitised volumes carry. He was a graduate student, so no class portrait grid holds him. His eyes are down on the animal he is handling; there is no other frame.
caption_quote: John Burden, a graduate assistant, does research on animal behavior using a Skinner rat cage.
how_identified: 1972 Talisman, printed p. 141 (scan leaf n144), the psychology department spread. The volume's captions point at the adjacent photograph with a direction word. This caption, set at the right of the page, reads 'Left-John Burden ...' and the photograph immediately to its left is a single man lifting a white rat out of a clear plexiglass box, which is the Skinner cage the caption describes. The only other caption on the page, set at the top, reads 'Left-Nancy Pape and Rick Rink conduct an experiment', names two people, and points across the gutter at the two-person photograph printed on p. 140, which was checked and does show two people at an apparatus. The Burden frame holds one person and the Pape and Rink frame holds two, so the two captions cannot be swapped. name: Buzz Smith
why: The only photograph of him in any digitised Talisman. The string 'Buzz Smith' occurs exactly once across the whole archive.org run 1963-1987, in this caption. Cropped from a two-man stage frame; the cap brim throws his eyes into shadow, which is why this is filed soft.
caption_quote: Bailiff Larry Heffington laughs it up on stage while “Chi O defendant” Buzz Smith waits in the witness box.
how_identified: 1979 Talisman, printed p. 316 (scan leaf n317), the lower-left photograph on the Fall Activities spread, showing SAE's November Nonsense skit about Chi Omega's effort to get a sorority house. Two men stand on a stage set lettered CITY COURT and the caption names two, Heffington then Smith, with a distinguishing action for each. Which is which is fixed twice over from inside the frame. The man on the left has his mouth wide open in mid-laugh and wears a star badge pinned to his chest, so he is the laughing bailiff, Larry Heffington. The man on the right wears a white cap lettered XΩ, the Greek letters of Chi Omega, and stands behind a rectangular white-outlined box with his hands clasped: he is the 'Chi O defendant' who 'waits in the witness box'. The badge and the cap are independent of each other and both point the same way, and neither man can be the other.

name: Sandra Tonjes
why: A clean studio portrait printed directly under a caption block that names her Associated Students office by name, and confirmed against a second captioned portrait of her two years earlier.
caption_quote: SANDRA SUE TONJES, Bowling Green, Ohio; Elementary Education; Chi Omega, treasurer, president; Associated Students, chairman rules and elections committee
how_identified: 1969 Talisman, part 1, printed p. 119 (PDF page 58 of tal1969-pt1), the Who's Who spread. Each entry is a block of biographical text set in a single column with its portrait immediately adjacent in the same column. Her column on the right-hand page reads, top to bottom: the TONJES text block, a woman's portrait, a man's portrait, then the WOODALL text block. There is no photograph above the TONJES text, so the only adjacency-consistent pairing in that column is TONJES to the woman above WOODALL's man, and both sexes match the printed given names, Sandra Sue and Gary H. The middle column of the same page is laid out identically and reads SCHUHMANN text, man, man, WHITLEY text, which confirms the nesting. Two independent checks then confirm the face. First, the caption itself names 'Associated Students, chairman rules and elections committee', which is the office the worklist gives her for 1967-68. Second, the same caption records her as Sweetheart of Kappa Sigma, and the 1967 Talisman's Kappa Sigma page, printed p. 184 (PDF page 94 of tal1967-pt1), prints a single female portrait with 'Sweetheart / SANDRA TONJES' set immediately beneath that one frame and no other person near it. The two faces are the same woman: the same short dark bob with a heavy straight fringe, the same face shape and the same smile, two years apart.

name: Steve Robinson

name: Frank Genzianelli

name: Dale Weaver
why: Cropped from a two-person frame, but the pairing cannot slide: the caption names one woman and one man and the photograph holds exactly one of each. This is the only clear frame of his face in the five volumes; the other three hits on him are large group photographs.

The same volume independently ties this Dale Weaver to student government twice: p. 70 prints him in the Associated Students group photograph caption, second row, and PDF page 47 of tal1967-pt2 gives the Sophomore Class Officers as 'Dave Whitaker, Representative-at-Large; Janice Dykes, Secretary; Terry Hicks, Vice President; Dale Weaver, President', which is the office the worklist gives him for 1966-67.

name: Bob Fox
why: His own senior class portrait. Small because the scan of this volume is 96 dpi and the grid runs four to a row.
caption_quote: EIGHTH ROW: Letha T. Fox, Elementary Education; Robert M. Fox, History; Sherry Coleman Fox, Elementary Education; Samuel S. Francis, Accounting
how_identified: 1969 Talisman, part 2, printed p. 275 (PDF page 39 in the file, PDF page 36 of tal1969-pt2), senior portraits. This volume captions by row and names the four people in each row in order, which removes the counting argument entirely: he is second in the eighth row, so row 8, column 2. All eight rows on the right-hand page were checked against their captions for sex and all eight match, and the male positions differ in every row, which fixes the alignment: row 1 woman, man, man, woman; row 2 man, woman, woman, woman; row 3 woman, woman, man, man; row 4 man, woman, man, man; row 5 man, man, woman, woman; row 6 woman, man, man, woman; row 7 man, woman, man, woman; row 8 woman, man, woman, man. Robert M. Fox is the only Robert or Bob Fox anywhere in the five volumes 1966-1970: every other male Fox in them is a Jim, Tim or Denny, and the Jim Fox of 1966-67 is a separate and well-documented person who was vice president of the Associated Students executive committee. This Robert Fox is listed as a member of Pi Kappa Alpha in both the 1967 and the 1968 volumes, and fraternity membership is a precondition of the Interfraternity Council seat the worklist gives Bob Fox for 1967-68. What is NOT in the volumes: no Talisman caption puts him on the Interfraternity Council. The council's own group photographs for 1966-67, 1967-68 and 1969-70 were all read and none names a Fox. The identification therefore rests on the uniqueness of the name in these years plus the fraternity membership, not on a caption.

name: Randi Jensen
why: Her own senior class portrait, and the volume that carries it is one year after the year she served. Small because the scan is 96 dpi and the grid runs four to a row.
caption_quote: SECOND ROW: Freddie Jeffries, English; Randi Jean Jensen, French; Brenda Kay Johnson, Mathematics, Spanish; Frederick Johnson, Biology
how_identified: 1969 Talisman, part 2, printed p. 281 (PDF page 39 of tal1969-pt2), senior portraits. All eight rows on the right-hand page were checked against their captions for sex and all eight match, with the male positions differing between rows: row 1 woman, man, woman, man; row 2 man, woman, woman, man; row 3 man, woman, woman, woman; row 4 man, woman, woman, woman; row 5 man, woman, woman, man; row 6 man, man, man, woman; row 7 man, man, man, woman; row 8 woman, man, woman, woman. Rows 1, 2 and 6 alone make the alignment unambiguous. The person is tied to student government independently of the name: the 1968 Talisman, printed p. 155 (PDF page 79 of tal1968), prints the Associated Students committee roster, and its publicity committee line begins 'Randi Jensen'. That is the same academic year, 1967-68, that the worklist gives her. She is the only Randi Jensen in the five volumes; the Marilee Jensen who appears in the 1967 volume is a different person.

name: Lowry Stagg
why: Cropped from a two-person Campus Favorites frame. It is the only photograph of her the archive can reach: 'Lowry Stagg' occurs exactly once in the five 1966-1970 volumes and nowhere in the 1971, 1972 or 1973 volumes on archive.org. The face is well lit and in focus, which is why it is worth cutting from a group.
caption_quote: Lowry Stagg and Ken Wood
how_identified: 1969 Talisman, part 2, printed p. 216 (PDF page 7 of tal1969-pt2), the upper photograph on the Campus Favorites closing page: a woman and a man sitting on a low brick wall. Three things fix which is which. First, the section's caption convention is left to right in the frame, not man-first: on the facing spread, printed pp. 214-215, four captions run 'Charlsie Malone and Tonii Rizzo' (woman left, man right), 'John Lee and Jennifer Taylor' (man left, woman right), 'Tyra Helsley and Sonny Murphy' (woman left, man right) and 'Gwen Tuell and Doug Nally' (woman left, man right), and the second caption on p. 216 itself, 'Mike Fletcher and Mary Morley', is man left and woman right. Five for five, and the order alternates by sex, so it cannot be a man-first rule. Second, Lowry Stagg is a woman: the same volume, part 1, printed p. 152, prints the Chi Omega membership list and 'Lowry Stagg' is in it, between Devon Stafford and Pam Sublitt. Third, Ken Wood is a man, named in the same volume as the Talisman's Honoraries Editor and listed in a fraternity roll. The frame holds one woman and one man, Stagg is named first, and first is the left. NOTE for a later pass: the Chi Omega page also carries a portrait grid, but it prints 39 portraits against 59 listed names and the name column runs at its own pitch and drifts a full row against the photograph rows, so that grid is NOT positionally countable and no portrait should be cut from it.

name: Steve Hunter
why: A clean studio portrait from his fraternity chapter page, the only page the 1971 volume gives him. He has no class portrait in any digitised volume.
caption_quote: Richard Garrett, Terry Hall, Chet Hogan, Steve Hunter.
how_identified: 1971 Talisman, printed p. 119 (scan leaf n278), the Sigma Phi Epsilon Kentucky Eta chapter page. Four portraits to a row with each row's names printed in a block set directly beside that row, in order. Hunter is fourth in the fourth block, so he is row 4, column 4. The page proves its own alignment twice over: the seven blocks name 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4 and 3 people and the grid holds exactly 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4 and 3 portraits, 27 against 27 with no slack anywhere; and after the four officers in block 1 and the social chairman who opens block 2, the remaining names run in strict alphabetical order, Beckley, Bennett, Burchett, Clark, Cunningham, Dockins, Evans, Garrett, Hall, Hogan, Hunter, Hurt, Krinsky, Lau, Logsdon, Lopez, Mann, Martin, Patchel, Stewart, Wilson, Young, so no block can be shifted. The 1971 back index carries one Steven Hunter, Steven Hughes Hunter, and gives him p. 119 and no other page. He is tied to student government by the 1970 volume, which prints him twice: printed p. 34 of part 1 gives the Associated Students executive committee as 'Standing: Steve Hunter, John Lyne, Paul Gerard, John Barra, David Porter; Sitting: Larry Zielke, Georganna Sleamaker', and part 2 gives the sophomore class officers as 'Joe Stark Gerard, Vice President; Steve Hunter, President; Marshall Galloway, Treasurer', which is the office the worklist gives him for 1969-70. The 1970 volume also lists him in the same fraternity roll as Dockins, Krinsky and Lau, which is the same chapter as this grid. NOTE: the sophomore class officers photograph itself was examined and rejected as a source. It holds four men and a woman and the caption names four men in one order, but the two men whose faces this archive already knows, Gerard and Galloway, do not sit in the caption's left-to-right order, so that frame's pairing is not provable at its print resolution.

name: Paul Gaines
why: A studio portrait from his fraternity chapter grid. It is small because the volume is scanned at 96 dpi and this grid runs seven portraits to a row; it has not been enlarged. He has no class portrait in any of the five volumes.
caption_quote: Ted DiGuiseppe, Steve Farmer, Randy Freeman, Jim Furey, Paul Gaines, Glenn Gardner, Jim Garrett
how_identified: 1969 Talisman, part 1, printed p. 175 (PDF page 86 of tal1969-pt1), the Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter page. Seven portraits to a row, with each row's seven names printed in a block set directly beside that row in order. Gaines is fifth in the second block, so he is row 2, column 5. The page proves its own alignment: nine blocks of exactly seven names each, 63 in all, against nine rows of exactly seven portraits, 63 in all, with no slack anywhere; and the names run in strict alphabetical order from Austin through Willis, so no block can be shifted by one. The person is tied to student government by the 1968 volume, printed p. 153 (PDF page 78 of tal1968), the Associated Students spread, whose group caption names 'Skip Gaines' in the fourth row under the officers Menser, Beck, Fowler and Heishman. Skip and Paul are the same man: the SAE officers caption on this very page reads 'Skip Gaines, Vice President', and the chapter's member grid beside it carries exactly one Gaines, Paul, so the nickname and the given name cannot be two people in one chapter. The worklist gives Paul Gaines as Sophomore Class Vice-President in 1967-68, the same year as that Associated Students photograph.

name: Bonnie Spinnogatti
why: Her own senior studio portrait from the class grid. Small because the volume scans at 96 dpi and the grid runs four portraits across; cut at 173 by 238 from a 2x render, not enlarged beyond that.
caption_quote: Bonnie Jo Spinogatti  Physical Education  Yonkers, N.Y.
how_identified: 1968 Talisman, printed p. 271 (PDF page 137 of tal1968.pdf, right half of the spread). The seniors section sets a four-across portrait grid with the names listed alongside in blocks of four, one block per row, left to right. Her block is the second: Danny L. Spillman, William P. Spinning, Bonnie Jo Spinogatti, Carol Sue Sprague, so she is the third portrait in the second row. The counting is not left to trust: the sexes in both the row above and her own row match their name blocks exactly. Row one reads Snider, Snider, Sowders, Spear = man, woman, man, woman, and the printed row is man, woman in glasses, man, woman. Her own row reads Spillman, Spinning, Spinogatti, Sprague = man, man, woman, woman, and the printed row is man in glasses, man, woman with long straight dark hair, woman with a dark bob. Position three is the only cell the block can put her in.
identification: PROVED. The Talisman prints Spinogatti with one n; the SGA roster prints Spinnogatti with two. It is one person, not two. The surname occurs exactly twice in 990 OCR'd pages of the 1966-1970 Talismans and both are her: this senior entry, and the Alpha Delta Pi chapter roster on PDF page 60 of the same volume. She is the only Spin(n)ogatti at Western in those five years. The other facts line up as well: the ASG officers' roster gives her campus address as Rodes-Harlin Hall, a women's residence hall, which is the constituency she represented, and the Talisman gives her home as Yonkers, N.Y., consistent with an out-of-state student living in a dorm. The same roster's ordering is independently verified by the officer directly above her, Randi Jensen, whose roster address is State Hall and who signs her Herald letter of 2 Nov 1967 'Randi Jensen, Publicity chairman, Associated Students, Junior, State Hall'.
spelling_note: Officers file and the WKU Archives roster read Spinnogatti. The 1968 Talisman prints Spinogatti. Flagged, not fixed; the entry uses the officers-file spelling.

name: George Carlson
why: A clean sophomore class studio portrait, 220 by 280, cut from a 3102-pixel archive.org page scan. Soft only from the halftone screen, not from downscaling.
caption_quote: GEORGIANA L. CARLSON, Des Plaines, Ill.
how_identified: 1977 Talisman, printed p. 387 (archive.org leaf n390), the Sophomores section. Nine portraits to a row with the nine names blocked alongside in order. Her block is the last on the page: Barbara A. Camp, Valerie B. Campbell, Mark A. Cannon, Catherine R. Cansler, Georgiana L. Carlson, Susan P. Carr, William S. Carrel, Carol A. Carroll, Laura R. Carson, so she is the fifth of nine. The row is checkable rather than merely countable: the block contains exactly two men, at positions three and seven, and the printed row carries exactly two men, at positions three and seven. Positions four, five and six were cut and compared and they run Black woman smiling, woman with short light hair, woman with long dark centre-parted hair, which is Cansler, Carlson, Carr in order. Column edges were found by brightness projection across the gutters rather than by eye.
identification: FACE PROVED, PERSON NOT PROVED - FOR THE EDITOR
identification_reasoning: The face is certainly Georgiana Lynn Carlson. What is NOT established is that she is the officers file's 'George Carlson'. FOR: the 1977 Talisman puts a Carlson inside ASG that very year - the ASG feature on printed p. 51 captions 'Christy Vogt, Bob Moore, Don Augenstein and Georgiana Carlson organize a rules and elec-tions committee' - and the volume's back index has no George Carlson at all, only 'Carlson, Georgiana Lynn 51, 267, 387' and 'Carlson, Gwen Axel'. The 1976 and 1978 back indexes agree: Georgiana Lynn Carlson at 1976 p. 300 and 1978 p. 330, and no George. That index lists students who were never photographed (Gwen Axel Carlson carries no page number at all), so a male George Carlson enrolled at Western ought to appear in it, and does not. AGAINST: 'George Carlson' is not a one-off slip, it is in print twice independently. The ASG minutes of 22 Feb 1977 name the convention nominee George Carlson, and the Herald of 12 Apr 1977 carries a letter from Tom Battle headed 'Wants George Carlson as Treasurer', so a George Carlson was a candidate in that spring's treasurer's race. Georgiana as 'George' is possible but is not something this archive can assert. years.json already records the doubt in its own note on the entry: whether the minutes' George Carlson is that person, or another, is not established. Two named ASG roles are involved - a convention nominee and a treasurer candidate on one side, a rules and elections committee member on the other - and nothing found here ties them to one body. An editor with the 22 Feb 1977 minutes in hand can settle it in a minute by checking whether the nominee's name is typed or handwritten and whether the same meeting seats Georgiana. Do not merge these two names on this evidence. LATE ADDITION, FOUND AFTER THIS ENTRY WAS FIRST WRITTEN AND IT MOVES THE BALANCE TOWARD ONE PERSON: years.json already carries Georgiana Carlson in its own right, and it records her as the LOSING CANDIDATE FOR ASG TREASURER in the April 1977 election as well as an organizer of that year's Rules and Elections committee. The Herald item that names a George is Tom Battle's letter of 12 Apr 1977, headed 'Wants George Carlson as Treasurer'. So the archive's own record of the 1977 treasurer's race has a Georgiana in it and the Herald's record of the same race has a George in it. That is the same contest, the same office and the same spring, which is a great deal harder to explain as two people than as one name written two ways. It still is not proof - a family could run two candidates and the archive's note on the George entry raises exactly that - but an editor should now be weighing 'one person' as the likelier reading rather than the other way round. Note also that the concurrent merge that ran during this session attached this crop to Georgiana Carlson, not to George Carlson, which is the correct destination for the face regardless of how the George question is settled.

name: David Young
why: Head and shoulders lifted out of a marching-band crowd photograph in the stands, 280 by 400 from a 3101-pixel archive.org scan. Not a studio portrait and never will be: he has no class portrait entry in the printed grids of the 1976, 1977, 1978 or 1979 volumes.
caption_quote: David Young, a sophomore from Bowling Green, enthusiastically cheers a play at the Tennessee Tech game.
how_identified: 1976 Talisman, printed p. 326 (archive.org leaf n329), the 'Band on the Run' feature, bottom right photograph. The same frame runs again on printed p. 260 over a cyan divider, which is why the back index gives him both pages; p. 326 is the clean black-and-white printing and is the one cut. The caption names exactly one person and describes exactly one action, and the frame contains exactly one person performing it: everyone else in the picture is seated, standing still or holding an instrument, while a single man in a bucket hat, glasses and Big Red Band T-shirt has both arms flung wide and his mouth wide open shouting. Within this photograph the identification is not a counting argument at all.
identification: FACE PROVED, PERSON NOT PROVED - FOR THE EDITOR
identification_reasoning: The face is certainly the David Young of this caption. Whether that David Young is the 1978-79 Administrative Vice President is the open question, and it turns on a chain the editor should judge rather than inherit. FOR: the 1976 volume's back index files this caption under 'Young, David Paul 260, 326', and the 1979 volume's back index files 'Young, David Paul 289' - and printed p. 289 of the 1979 volume is where the ASG story quotes 'David Young, administrative vice president'. Same indexed identity, same middle name, three years apart. The 1979 index also lists no other plain David Young; the second one who existed in 1977, 'Young, David Wayne 277, 415', is gone from the 1979 book. AGAINST: the 1979 index's attribution is the indexer's own inference. All the running text on p. 289 gives is the bare words 'David Young', and an indexer matching that against the student directory would land on the only David Young in it whether or not that is who the reporter meant. And the arithmetic is uncomfortable: a sophomore in 1975-76 is in a fifth year by 1978-79. That is common enough not to disprove anything, but it is not nothing. VERIFICATION THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: any ASG document of 1978-79 giving the administrative vice president's class year, hometown or middle initial. Bowling Green and a middle name of Paul would close it in one line.
